decisions.normalizedClaim: Rick Hansen supports requiring refinery facilities to notify local first responders of hazardous chemical releases.
decisions.supportingExcerpt: Finally, I introduced bipartisan legislation requiring refinery facilities to notify local first responders of hazardous chemical releases in their area, ensuring folks on the ground can address public health concerns.

decisions.normalizedClaim: Natalie Zeleznikar supports adjusting electric-vehicle registration fees so EV drivers contribute more comparably to road funding.
decisions.supportingExcerpt: In the Transportation Committee I also introduced House File 189. HF 189 is designed to create parity between traditional gas-powered vehicles and electric vehicles (EVs) in funding Minnesota’s roads and bridges.

decisions.normalizedClaim: María Isa Pérez-Vega opposes the governor's return-to-office mandate for state employees and supports state-worker telework agreements.
decisions.supportingExcerpt: I oppose this decision and stand in strong support of MAPE and AFSCME members, who are rightfully denouncing Governor Walz's unilateral revocation of telework agreements.

decisions.normalizedClaim: Julie Greene supports protecting the rights of LGBTQ and immigrant communities from discriminatory government action.
decisions.supportingExcerpt: I will fight to protect the rights of communities already marginalized, particularly our LGBQT and immigrant neighbors.

decisions.normalizedClaim: Bianca Ward Virnig supports comprehensive and compassionate services for people with disabilities.
decisions.supportingExcerpt: Our community's commitment to disability rights is unwavering, and I will continue to fight for comprehensive, compassionate support for individuals with disabilities.

decisions.normalizedClaim: Cedrick Frazier supports standardized traffic-stop protocols intended to prevent racial profiling and unnecessary escalation.
decisions.supportingExcerpt: Traffic Stop Reform Last week, I introduced legislation to ensure that every Minnesotan is treated equitably no matter their race or where they live by establishing clear, consistent protocols that prevent racial profiling and unnecessary escalations during traffic stops.

decisions.normalizedClaim: Nathan Coulter supports prohibiting former legislators from becoming lobbyists for two years after leaving office.
decisions.supportingExcerpt: I also introduced legislation to prohibit legislators from becoming lobbyists for two years after leaving office.

decisions.normalizedClaim: Matt Bliss supports eliminating Minnesota's duty to retreat when a person uses reasonable force in lawful self-defense.
decisions.supportingExcerpt: That’s why I introduced House File 13 , which would eliminate the duty to retreat when using reasonable force in self-defense or in defense of others.

decisions.normalizedClaim: Peter Fischer opposes rolling back Minnesota's PFAS prevention measures.
decisions.supportingExcerpt: I voted No on this bill to roll back PFAS prevention measures because our communities' health, environment, and infrastructure are more important than corporate profits.

decisions.normalizedClaim: Steve Elkins supports easing zoning rules to allow more housing construction and improve housing affordability.
decisions.supportingExcerpt: This legislation would ease some zoning rules so that our cities can build more housing. Our restrictive zoning laws have a detrimental effect on affordability which leads to a whole lot of downstream issues.
